docs.title: INT. OBSERVATION BOX -- MORNING
beats: A swallowtail rises into the clear acrylic lid of a choice maze and strikes it.
It falls, rights itself in air, and strikes again. The roof offers no resistance until contact.
Below, lavender divides the world: one corridor carries it, the other does not.
Sugar water is on BOTH arms. The only variable is memory.
The choice interval has run 43 seconds and should have ended after 30. It does not choose.
An untrained animal splits evenly. A trained one avoids the scented arm about seven times in ten. This one does neither.
el: I remember the roof as a brightness I could not enter.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · MONITOR -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The software draws the flight path as a green line.
The line gathers over itself, loop after loop.
A figure appears: an almost closed circle crossed near its lower edge by a crooked stroke.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Niko presses the manual switch. Fans sigh. The lavender thins into the extraction hood.
The butterfly continues its pattern regardless.
Mara has not moved. Her hands are still inside the sleeves of the observation box.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · THE BENCH -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The butterfly passes over her wrist before she can lower the vial.
Its feet touch her skin: not pressure but arrangement — six points becoming twelve, twelve becoming none.
It lifts and strikes the ceiling once more. A yellow powder remains on her glove.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · THE PARTITION -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The swallowtail settles on the white partition between the two corridors.
Its wings close, opening the false eyes on their undersides.
The eyes look backward.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · MONITOR -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Mara asks for the path visualization to be deleted from the report.
Niko discovers a loose wire and cannot yet tell whether it is live.
el: The arm choice is the record.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · HER HAND -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Yellow scales have passed through a puncture near the thumb and settled on her skin.
They lie in the lines of her palm like ground metal.
She rubs them with the side of her finger. Instead of disappearing, they brighten.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · THE TALL WINDOWS -- MORNING
beats: The laboratory occupies the upper floor of a converted textile mill; the windows are too tall for modern use.
Water towers, apartment roofs, the white rind of a stadium appear not outside but preserved within the glass.
The butterfly room once housed looms. Their floor bolts remain — dark circles surrounded by rust.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · THE CABINET -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Four people stand outside a glasshouse whose windows have been painted white for blackout.
A woman in a pale dress holds a shallow wooden tray of chrysalides, each tied upright to a narrow card.
Someone has drawn a mark above one child's head: a broken circle with a stroke through its lower edge.
el: The woman is supposed to be my grandmother.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · THE REVERSE -- CONTINUOUS
beats: On the back, in blue fountain pen: ASTER HOUSE / AUGUST 1945 / IONA, ELISE, THOMAS / DO NOT TURN AROUND.
Below the writing is the same broken circle. The ink has faded from black to brown but the shape is clean.
el: She said she remembered being there.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY -- CONTINUOUS
beats: A closed loop of question and concession that returns exactly to where it began.
Every answer is yes. Nothing is resolved by any of them.
el: Could it have gotten into the intake?
The sensor would have caught it.
Then why are we looking at a photograph from 1945?

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · THE VIAL -- CONTINUOUS
beats: One hindwing is damaged. A small crescent has been removed from its edge, as neatly as if cut with a punch.
Through the missing portion, the white card behind shows with impossible brightness.
There is nothing sharp in the maze.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · THE PHONE -- CONTINUOUS
beats: For several seconds there is only breathing — a larger rhythm, rough and receding, like water dragged over stone.
An old woman's voice arrives from a number Mara does not know.
el: You always open it too early. Your mother did. Her mother did. The insects wake before the story is ready for them.
I found the boy. He has been dead for eleven years.

docs.title: INT. LABORATORY · RECOVERY RACK -- CONTINUOUS
beats: From the recovery rack comes a dry tapping.
The butterfly strikes the vial once, then again. Not wildly.
It moves around the circumference, testing the glass at equal intervals.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE FIRE DOOR -- CONTINUOUS
beats: A smell rises from the stairwell — not the measured concentration of the maze.
This is green and bitter. Crushed stems warming in a hand.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE STAIRCASE -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Light enters from windows at each landing and falls in long dusty columns.
Mara moves down through them, one after another.
A strip of red satin slides across her shoe like a tongue.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE LOBBY -- NOON
beats: A small woman in a navy coat with a flattened fur collar, holding a grocery bag darkened at the bottom.
Lavender protrudes from it in a thick bundle.
She looks not up the stairs but at their reflection in the glass door.
Her face has an unfinished quality — expressions arriving before the features can contain them.
el: That depends which paper you're reading.
Yes. That was what made it difficult.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE LOBBY -- CONTINUOUS
beats: A dented circular canister no wider than her palm. Rust spreads from the hinge in branching lines.
Around the edge, black electrical tape. Beneath the rust, a fragment of white label: ASTER.
Yellow scales cling to the tape, caught in the adhesive. They are fresh enough to shine.
el: Was there a butterfly in it?

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE LOBBY -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Niko reaches for the canister. Mara moves it away from him.
The gesture is small. It enters the room like a confession.
el: You work for the clean version.
This is exactly how contamination happens.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE GLASS DOOR -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Through the glass the street stands white in the noon heat. A bus passes.
For an instant its windows reflect the mill's brick façade, and the lobby appears occupied by rows of seated people moving backward.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE LOBBY FLOOR -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The canister clicks. All three hear it.
The sound comes again, faint and exact. Not metal contracting.
Something taps from inside, moving around the circumference at equal intervals.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE LOBBY -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Iona catches Mara's wrist. Her hand is unexpectedly strong.
At the base of her thumb is a scar: a broken circle crossed by a crooked line.
el: The first time you see it, you will think the picture is remembering the event.
The second time, you will think the event was arranged to resemble the picture.
Do not watch it a third time.
Because then you will remember being there.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE OPEN CANISTER -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Inside: a coil of 8mm film wrapped in waxed paper, and a dry chrysalis resting in the hollow centre of the reel.
Larger than any swallowtail chrysalis Mara has seen. Split along one side. Empty.
A black leg appears beneath the film, withdraws, appears again.
The butterfly pushes upward through a nest of its own discarded history.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE REEL -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Across the left hindwing the scales form a pale broken circle. No line crosses it.
The butterfly raises its wings. On the right hindwing is the line.
The mark exists only when the wings are closed together.
It opens: the symbol divides. It closes: the symbol becomes whole.
el: Now you understand why it cannot be photographed.
Of course it can be photographed.

docs.title: INT. MILL · THE ENTRANCE DOOR -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The butterfly climbs the white brightness of the door. Impact. Drop. Recovery.
The orange cup breaks without drama, pieces sliding apart over the stone.
Niko shoves the crash bar. Heat, traffic, hot rubber, river damp, cut weeds, diesel, sunlight.
The butterfly passes into all of it and vanishes above the awning.

docs.title: EXT. SERVICE ALLEY -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The butterfly turns at the alley's end. Therefore they turn.
It crosses a fenced lot where waist-high weeds have grown through the chassis of a delivery truck.
Iona is fast for perhaps twenty paces. Then her body remembers its age.

docs.title: EXT. THE LOT · THE SPILLED LAVENDER -- CONTINUOUS
docs.place: EXT. THE LOT · THE SPILLED LAVENDER
beats: The bag splits, releasing lavender stems across the pavement.
The butterfly descends and touches one flower. It does not recoil.
el: This one has the same marking.

docs.title: EXT. THE WAREHOUSE · PLYWOOD -- CONTINUOUS
beats: A low brick structure attached to the rear of the warehouse, windows covered in plywood.
On the nearest board, painted: a broken circle with a line through it. The paint is new.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Clear plastic sheeting divides the loading room into narrow chambers. Tubes run along the floor. Fans turn behind filters.
Hundreds of chrysalides hang from cards along the far wall. Each card bears a date: 1951, 1952, 1953, 1954, 1955.
The oldest cards are brown and soft at the corners. The newest are clean white plastic.
Every chrysalis, old or new, is fastened identically: a loop of silk around the thorax, a drop of adhesive beneath the tail.
el: This is the part that keeps reappearing.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE TILED POOL -- CONTINUOUS
docs.place: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE TILED POOL
beats: A shallow tiled pool at the centre. Lavender grows in galvanized troughs around its edge.
A projector stands on a wheeled cart. Its power light is on. Opposite, a white rectangle waits.
el: Someone has been running experiments here.
Enough to keep it from becoming evidence.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE FILM IN HER HAND -- CONTINUOUS
docs.place: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE FILM IN HER HAND
beats: She holds the strip toward the fluorescent light and advances it between her fingers.
The child straightens. The woman turns. The butterfly descends.
Then the image changes: the next frame shows Mara herself standing in the lobby with the canister in her hands.
She drops the film. Niko catches it. He lifts it to the light and sees only the glasshouse.
el: You saw yourself arranged as a memory.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE WALL -- CONTINUOUS
beats: A clicking comes from the wall. One chrysalis moves. Then another. The sound travels down the rows.
Each seam splits at once — a synchronized line passing across the wall from left to right.
The oldest open first. Empty. Then the next. Empty. Every chrysalis is empty.
Yet the wall continues to move: something passes through the husks without occupying them, a distortion like wind crossing tall grass.
el: You have to give me something.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE PROJECTION -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The projector turns on. Its fan rises to speed. Light strikes the wall.
No one has threaded the film. Nevertheless an image appears.
A glasshouse. White-painted windows. Lavender beside a pool. Three children with their backs to the camera.
A woman enters carrying a tray of chrysalides. Mara knows her before she turns — not her face. Her shoulders.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The sound comes from behind her.
Not the voice thinned by medication and made formal by the effort to appear lucid.
This is the voice from childhood — impatient and amused, calling from the front seat while Mara knelt backward in the car to watch a storm disappear behind them.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE WALL -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Mara turns. Therefore the film changes.
She now sees the laboratory lobby: Iona handing her the canister, Niko dropping the orange cup, the butterfly striking the door.
Within the projected image, the small projected Mara turns toward the camera. Her lips move. This time there is sound.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE POOL -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The reel slips and rolls in a widening circle across the floor, film unwinding behind it.
It strikes the tiled edge and falls into the water. Therefore the strip tightens.
Therefore every frame between the cart and the water becomes briefly visible:

A man raising his hand. A woman in a green dress. A burning barn. A hotel corridor. A child on an airport platform. A face reflected in an artificial eye. A car sinking through blue light. A witness pointing across a courtroom. A dead wife opening her eyes on a space station.

docs.title: INT. THE MAZE · THE BUTTERFLY'S VIEW -- CONTINUOUS
docs.place: INT. THE MAZE · THE BUTTERFLY'S VIEW
beats: The projection cuts to a butterfly beating against a transparent ceiling — the same trial from that morning.
But the viewpoint is inside the maze.
Mara sees herself beyond the acrylic: enormous, distorted, holding her breath.
The butterfly strikes the lid. The image goes white.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY · DARKNESS -- CONTINUOUS
beats: Every fluorescent tube goes out. Darkness arrives complete except for the projector beam.
Within it, scales drift. Thousands of them.
They move across the light in slow currents, each scale briefly becoming a bright rectangle — a frame too small to contain the event it had carried.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY · DARKNESS -- CONTINUOUS
beats: The memory enters through no opening she can name. Not a vision. Not information. A pressure toward action.
She knows a child stands behind her at the edge of the pool.
She knows the child will fall if she does not turn. She knows turning will cause the glass above them to break.
She knows her mother stood in this position. She knows Iona did. She knows none of these things can all be true.

docs.title: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE POOL'S EDGE -- CONTINUOUS
docs.place: INT. REARING FACILITY · THE POOL'S EDGE
beats: At the pool's edge stands a girl in a yellow dress. Water streams from her hair.
In both hands she holds a chrysalis split neatly along one side. She looks eight years old.
She has Mara's face. She raises the empty chrysalis to her ear.
Then the projector stops. In the darkness, something opens its wings.

chars.name: The Girl in the Yellow Dress

concepts.name: THE BROKEN CIRCLE
concepts.gloss: A shape that only completes when two halves are brought together, and which appears in flight path, photograph, scar, wing and new paint.

concepts.name: TRANSFER
concepts.gloss: A substance that moves between surfaces without changing: butterfly to glove to skin to tape to film to the beam. It brightens rather than fades when rubbed.

concepts.name: REFUSAL
concepts.gloss: Rejecting the premise rather than the options. The insect does not choose an arm; it strikes the ceiling.

concepts.name: TRANSPARENCY
concepts.gloss: A barrier that offers no resistance until the instant of contact. Mistaking transparency for permission.

concepts.name: RECURRENCE
concepts.gloss: The part that keeps reappearing. Three generations opening the lavender too early.

concepts.name: DO NOT TURN AROUND
concepts.gloss: The instruction that governs the whole text, written on a photograph in 1945 and spoken aloud in the dark.

concepts.name: WAKING TOO EARLY
concepts.gloss: The insects wake before the story is ready for them. Empty chrysalides that still move.

concepts.name: THE CLEAN VERSION
concepts.gloss: The record that omits the path. Deleting the visualization while keeping the trial.

concepts.name: CONTAINMENT
concepts.gloss: Sealed things that tap from inside. Tape, vials, canisters, plastic sheeting, glass.

concepts.name: PRESERVATION
concepts.gloss: Windows that hold the city rather than showing it. Factories pretending they have forgotten what they made.

concepts.name: THE EYES LOOK BACKWARD
concepts.gloss: False eyes on the underside of a wing. Being observed by the thing you are observing.

concepts.name: ADVANCE
concepts.gloss: Frames stepping past a gate one at a time — film, landings, corridors of light.

concepts.name: ACCUMULATION
concepts.gloss: A figure that only appears after enough time has passed over itself.

concepts.name: DAMAGE
concepts.gloss: A crescent removed as neatly as if cut with a punch, from a place nothing sharp could reach.

concepts.name: THE KINDEST AVAILABLE SMELL
concepts.gloss: Lavender is in the corridor because a child refused to use a killing agent. The mercy and the injury are the same molecule.

concepts.name: 物化 · THE TRANSFORMATION OF THINGS
concepts.gloss: Zhuangzi's word for what a chrysalis does, and for the distinction that must exist between the dreamer and the dreamt. A wall of dated husks is a wall of wuhua, every one of them empty.

concepts.name: IT HAS BEEN DONE BEFORE
concepts.gloss: Someone ran this experiment already, was doubted, and is still alive to arrive carrying the film. Your colony was taught.

concepts.name: NEITHER FIFTY NOR SEVENTY
concepts.gloss: The two real results are 50/50 and 70/30. This animal produces a third that is in no dataset: it declines the question. Only legible against the two it refuses.
